content.clinicalSnapshot: ⟦NAME_OF_PATIENT_MANY⟧ presents with recurrent unexpected panic attacks approximately twice weekly, accompanied by avoidance of highway driving and reluctance to speak at work. Anxiety symptoms are the dominant feature, with mild social anxiety compounding occupational functioning. Alcohol use beyond intended limits on weekends, with two failed attempts to cut down, suggests a developing pattern of misuse that may interact with current benzodiazepine use. The patient maintains a stable common-law relationship and close friendships, which serve as meaningful supports. No depressive episode, trauma history or suicidal ideation was identified on structured assessment.

diagnoses.name: Panic Disorder
diagnoses.rationale: This diagnosis accounts for the central presenting complaint of recurrent unexpected panic attacks with palpitations, breathlessness and fear of dying. Highway driving avoidance reflects the behavioural impact. Attacks occur approximately twice weekly.

evidence.quote: The patient meets DSM-5 criteria for Panic Disorder with moderate severity.
The patient reports unexpected panic attacks about twice a week with palpitations, breathlessness and fear of dying, and avoids driving on highways.

dsmEvidence.quote: Panic Disorder is recorded as DSM-5-TR F41.0 and ICD-11 6B01.

diagnoses.name: Social Anxiety Disorder
diagnoses.rationale: Fear of judgement in meetings and avoidance of speaking at work adds a second anxiety diagnosis that compounds occupational difficulty. Symptoms are mild but functionally relevant.

evidence.quote: The patient meets DSM-5 criteria for Social Anxiety Disorder with mild severity.
The patient reports fear of being judged in meetings and avoids speaking up at work.

diagnoses.name: Alcohol Use Disorder
diagnoses.rationale: Weekend drinking beyond intended amounts and two unsuccessful attempts to reduce intake meet criteria for a mild alcohol use disorder. This pattern is clinically relevant given concurrent benzodiazepine use.

evidence.quote: The patient meets DSM-5 criteria for Alcohol Use Disorder with mild severity.

qualifiers.text: Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder was ruled out. Checking behaviour was endorsed but does not occupy more than one hour daily and does not cause marked distress, falling below the clinical threshold.
Posttraumatic Stress Disorder was ruled out. No exposure to a traumatic event meeting Criterion A was identified.
Major Depressive Disorder was ruled out. Low mood on some days was endorsed, but loss of interest was absent, and full criteria were not met.

treatmentReference.treatmentOptions: Cognitive behavioural therapy (CBT) with interoceptive exposure; psychoeducation and graded in-vivo exposure for agoraphobic avoidance
treatmentReference.medicationClasses: Selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors; serotonin-norepinephrine reuptake inhibitors
treatmentReference.planningConsiderations: First line, psychological: cognitive behavioural therapy with panic-focused exposure. Medication is second line and may be considered where therapy alone is declined, unavailable or insufficient.

treatmentReference.treatmentOptions: Cognitive behavioural therapy (CBT) including graded exposure to feared social situations
treatmentReference.medicationClasses: Selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors; serotonin-norepinephrine reuptake inhibitors
treatmentReference.planningConsiderations: First line, psychological: cognitive behavioural therapy with social-exposure components. Medication is second line where psychological treatment is insufficient or unavailable.

treatmentReference.treatmentOptions: Motivational interviewing; brief interventions; cognitive behavioural relapse prevention
treatmentReference.planningConsiderations: First line, psychological: motivational interviewing and brief intervention for mild alcohol use disorder. Medication is generally reserved for moderate-to-severe presentations. Address concurrent benzodiazepine-alcohol co-use as a safety priority.

content.interactionNote: The patient reports current lorazepam use alongside regular alcohol consumption. This co-occurrence is flagged in the Medication interaction risk row. Confirm lorazepam dose, frequency and prescriber oversight before initiating any additional pharmacotherapy for Panic Disorder or Alcohol Use Disorder.
content.limitations: Findings are based on structured self-report interviews completed on the assessment date and reflect the patient's presentation at that time. Suicide risk is dynamic and this letter does not predict future behaviour. Occupation, psychotherapy history and hospitalisation history were not reported in the case materials. The lorazepam dose and frequency were not specified; confirm these details with the prescribing clinic.
